title: Unbounded K-flat replacements from functorial flat resolutions
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with a monoidal structure $(\otimes,\mathbf 1)$ [def-sfb-monoidal-category] whose tensor product is additive in each variable. Colimits are as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; countable coproducts mean colimits over countable discrete categories, and $\mathbf Z$-indexed colimits mean colimits over the ordered set $(\mathbf Z,\leq)$. Assume countable coproducts exist, $\mathbf Z$-indexed colimits exist and their colimit functor preserves short exact sequences, and tensoring on either side with any fixed object preserves both those coproducts and those colimits. A flat object means an object whose tensor functors on both sides preserve short exact sequences. Assume there is a functor $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ with flat values and a natural epimorphism $P\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$. For every unbounded cochain complex $K$ in $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], there are a K-flat complex $Q$ [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] and a quasi-isomorphism $q:Q\to K$.

source.place: first paragraph, existence of K-flat resolutions under the general monoidal hypotheses; supporting source code: WeilConjectures.FromJoel.CategoryTheory.Abelian.Flat.KFlat, lines 378–437

proof.text: Countable coproducts provide the binary graded tensor colimits. Preservation of countable coproducts by tensorLeft and tensorRight provides HasGoodTensor₁₂Tensor, HasGoodTensorTensor₂₃ and HasTensor₄ObjExt: after introducing the two integer indices each is preservation of a coproduct over a subtype of a finite product of integers. Consequently the source monoidal structure on cochain complexes is available. Its two-sided kFlat predicate is definitionally equal to IsKFlatForTotalTensor, since its tensor maps are the same binary direct-sum total tensor maps.

Define a LeftResolution of the inclusion of flat objects by F = ObjectProperty.lift flat P hP and augmentation ε. Every component is epic by hypothesis. Flat objects contain zero and are closed under finite biproducts and retracts, as supplied by the source KFlat module. Set Γ = Λ.reduced, the explicit idempotent-completion construction of LeftResolution/Reduced.lean. It still takes values in flat objects and has epic augmentation, and Γ.F preserves zero morphisms. This requires no additivity of the given P.

source.place: LeftResolution.reduced and instPreservesZeroMorphismsFReduced, applied to the flat full subcategory.

proof.text: Take Q = Γ.resolutionFunctor.obj K and q = Γ.resolutionNatTrans.app K, using the existing source construction in FromJoel/Algebra/Homology/LeftResolution/CochainComplex.lean. This constructs bounded-above resolutions by termwise resolution and totalization, and extends to all complexes along the ordered-integer good-truncation filtration. The source instance quasiIso_resolutionNatTrans_app proves QuasiIso q from exactness of the integer colimit. The source theorem Γ.kFlat_resolutionFunctor_obj flat.essImage_ι_le K proves that Q is two-sided K-flat: its proof applies the bounded-above-flat criterion to its stages and the proved closedUnderColimitsOfShape_kFlat instance to their colimit. The tensor-preservation hypotheses here are exactly those required by these source results.
